title: VCRI People Asset Assessment Methodology v1

grades.meaning: Best-in-class people-security posture. Documented, enforced, and attested controls across all dimensions. Vetted workforce, phishing-resistant authentication, least privilege, mature insider-threat program. No critical findings.
Solid people-security posture. Documented controls across most dimensions; minor gaps in 1-2 areas with remediation paths defined. Suitable for production trust with stated caveats.
Acceptable with conditions. Notable gaps in 2-3 dimensions; remediation roadmap required. Not suitable for high-trust privileged operations without compensating controls.
Significant gaps across multiple dimensions. Workforce risk is material; remediation required before privileged trust.
Material failure of people-security posture. Privileged trust not recommended in current state.

subcriteria.title: Personnel vetting and background screening
anchors: No vetting of personnel or contractors before granting access; identity and history unverified.
Screening performed ad-hoc for some roles; no defined standard or record.
A screening standard (background checks, identity verification) is defined but inconsistently applied across roles and contractors.
Documented vetting standard consistently applied to all in-scope personnel and contractors before access, with records retained.
All of #3 plus risk-tiered screening (deeper checks for privileged roles), periodic re-screening, and audit of completion.
All of #4 plus continuous-evaluation programs for high-trust roles and independently attested screening coverage.

subcriteria.title: User behavioral baselining
anchors: No understanding of normal user behavior; no baselines exist.
Behavioral observation is ad-hoc and manual on a few accounts only.
A baselining approach is defined but inconsistently deployed; coverage is partial.
Behavioral baselines documented and consistently maintained for in-scope users (login patterns, access norms).
All of #3 plus UEBA tooling deployed org-wide with anomaly scoring and audited coverage.
All of #4 plus statistical behavioral models with continuous anomaly scoring and independently validated detection efficacy.

subcriteria.title: Individual accountability and no shared accounts
anchors: Shared and generic accounts are common; actions cannot be attributed to individuals.
Individual accounts used in some areas; shared accounts persist without controls.
A no-shared-account standard is defined but inconsistently enforced; exceptions are untracked.
Individual accountability documented and consistently enforced; shared accounts eliminated or tightly controlled and logged.
All of #3 plus automated detection of shared-account usage and audited exception handling.
All of #4 plus cryptographically attributable individual sessions and independently verified accountability.

subcriteria.title: Authentication strength
anchors: Password-only or shared credentials; no multi-factor authentication.
MFA enabled ad-hoc for some users or systems; coverage is partial and inconsistent.
An MFA standard is defined but inconsistently applied across the workforce and applications.
MFA documented and consistently enforced for all in-scope interactive access.
All of #3 plus adaptive/risk-based authentication, enforced credential policy, and audited authentication logs.
All of #4 plus phishing-resistant/passwordless authentication (FIDO2/WebAuthn) and independently attested identity controls.

subcriteria.title: Identity lifecycle: joiners, movers, leavers
anchors: No defined process for provisioning or deprovisioning access; access lingers after role change or departure.
Joiner/mover/leaver handled manually and ad-hoc; delays and orphaned accounts common.
A lifecycle process is defined but inconsistently followed; timeliness is not measured.
Documented joiner/mover/leaver process consistently applied; access changes tracked to role changes.
All of #3 plus automated provisioning/deprovisioning, periodic access recertification, and audited timeliness.
All of #4 plus event-driven lifecycle automation with independently attested zero-orphan-account assurance.

subcriteria.title: Single sign-on and federation
anchors: Credentials are siloed per application; no central identity.
SSO used for a few applications ad-hoc; most access uses separate credentials.
An SSO/federation standard is defined but inconsistently adopted across applications.
Centralized identity (SSO/federation) documented and consistently applied to in-scope applications.
All of #3 plus enforced federation policy, centralized session control, and audited coverage.
All of #4 plus near-complete federation with continuous session governance and independently attested centralization.

subcriteria.title: Consent and personal-data handling by staff
anchors: Staff handle personal data with no consent awareness or handling rules.
Some handling guidance exists informally; consent is assumed and untracked.
A personal-data handling and consent policy is defined but inconsistently followed by staff.
Documented handling rules and consent practices consistently applied by the in-scope workforce.
All of #3 plus technical guardrails on staff access to personal data and audited adherence.
All of #4 plus enforced purpose-bound access for staff with independently validated handling compliance.

subcriteria.title: Workforce privacy controls
anchors: No controls limiting staff access to personal data to what their role requires.
Role-based limits applied ad-hoc; broad staff access to personal data common.
A least-access standard for personal data is defined but inconsistently enforced for the workforce.
Documented role-scoped access to personal data consistently enforced across staff.
All of #3 plus periodic recertification of staff access to personal data and audited over-access detection.
All of #4 plus just-in-time access to sensitive personal data and independently attested minimization.

subcriteria.title: Privacy training and awareness
anchors: No privacy training; staff are unaware of obligations.
Privacy mentioned ad-hoc in onboarding only; no recurring program.
A privacy training program is defined but inconsistently delivered or tracked.
Documented recurring privacy training consistently delivered to the in-scope workforce with completion tracked.
All of #3 plus role-tailored privacy training, comprehension testing, and audited completion.
All of #4 plus adaptive training triggered by behavior/events with independently measured effectiveness.

subcriteria.title: Privileged access management and least privilege
anchors: Users routinely operate with standing administrative privilege; no PAM.
Some privileged accounts managed ad-hoc; broad standing admin rights common.
A least-privilege/PAM standard is defined but inconsistently enforced; standing privilege persists.
Least privilege documented and consistently enforced; privileged accounts managed through a PAM solution.
All of #3 plus just-in-time elevation, session recording, privilege analytics, and audited grants.
All of #4 plus zero standing privilege and independently attested least-privilege enforcement.

subcriteria.title: Security awareness and anti-phishing training
anchors: No security-awareness training; staff are untested against phishing.
Annual awareness content delivered ad-hoc; no phishing simulation or measurement.
An awareness program is defined but inconsistently delivered; phishing tests run rarely.
Documented recurring awareness program with phishing simulations consistently delivered and tracked.
All of #3 plus measured click/report rates, adaptive training triggered by failures, and audited improvement trends.
All of #4 plus continuous behavioral coaching with independently validated reduction in susceptibility.

subcriteria.title: Insider-threat and social-engineering resistance
anchors: No insider-threat program; social-engineering attempts succeed without friction.
Insider risk handled reactively and ad-hoc; no defined controls (e.g., callback verification).
Insider-threat and verification controls are defined but inconsistently applied.
Documented insider-threat controls (verification procedures, dual control for sensitive actions) consistently applied.
All of #3 plus behavioral risk indicators monitored, escalation paths exercised, and audited control adherence.
All of #4 plus predictive insider-risk analytics with independently validated program effectiveness.

subcriteria.title: Role clarity and segregation of duties
anchors: Roles and responsibilities are undefined; anyone can perform any sensitive action.
Roles described informally; segregation of duties applied ad-hoc where convenient.
A role/SoD model is defined but inconsistently enforced; conflicting duties common.
Documented roles with segregation of duties for sensitive functions consistently enforced.
All of #3 plus automated SoD-conflict detection, periodic review, and audited enforcement.
All of #4 plus continuous SoD monitoring with independently attested conflict-free assignment.

subcriteria.title: Competency and security-training currency
anchors: No requirement that staff in security-relevant roles hold or maintain relevant competency.
Competency expectations exist informally; currency is not tracked.
A competency/training-currency standard is defined but inconsistently maintained.
Documented competency requirements for security-relevant roles consistently maintained and tracked.
All of #3 plus measured currency, gap remediation, and audited training completion for in-scope roles.
All of #4 plus continuously managed competency with independently verified currency.

subcriteria.title: Key-person risk, succession, and coverage
anchors: Critical functions depend on single individuals with no backup or documentation.
Key-person risk recognized informally; mitigation is ad-hoc.
A coverage/succession standard is defined but inconsistently applied; single points of human failure persist.
Documented cross-training, backup coverage, and succession for critical functions consistently maintained.
All of #3 plus tested coverage (planned absence drills), runbook currency, and audited coverage gaps.
All of #4 plus resilient, regularly exercised succession with independently validated continuity.

subcriteria.title: User activity monitoring
anchors: User activity on systems and data is not logged or monitored.
Some user activity logged ad-hoc; logs unreviewed and not centralized.
A user-activity monitoring standard is defined but inconsistently applied; coverage has gaps.
User activity logging documented and consistently enabled across in-scope systems, centrally collected.
All of #3 plus alerting on anomalous user activity (SIEM/UEBA), tamper-resistant logs, and audited coverage.
All of #4 plus behavioral analytics on all human activity with validated detection coverage and independent attestation.

subcriteria.title: Insider-threat detection and response
anchors: No capability or plan to detect or respond to malicious or negligent insider activity.
Insider incidents handled improvised; no documented plan or roles.
An insider-threat response plan is defined but untested and inconsistently understood.
Documented insider-threat detection and response plan (roles, containment, HR/legal coordination) consistently maintained.
All of #3 plus tested response, insider-specific detection use cases, and audited readiness.
All of #4 plus regularly exercised response with measured detection/response times and independently validated readiness.

subcriteria.title: Offboarding and access-revocation integrity
anchors: Departing personnel retain access; revocation is unreliable or skipped.
Offboarding done manually and ad-hoc; delays and missed systems common.
An offboarding standard is defined but inconsistently executed; completeness unverified.
Documented offboarding consistently executed with timely revocation across in-scope systems.
All of #3 plus automated revocation, completeness verification, and audited offboarding timeliness.
All of #4 plus event-driven immediate revocation with independently attested zero-residual-access assurance.
